diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: Shahram Khaledi highlighted that the main difference in the new US sanctions campaign is the active naval blockade and the denial of dollar transactions. He mentioned the expansion of secondary sanctions to chains related to transactions with the Islamic Republic. The use of cryptocurrencies as a sanction tool was also noted.

Houshang Hasan-Yari pointed to increasing economic, military, and political pressures by the US against the Islamic Republic. He said we are gradually entering a phase where war will be inevitable. He predicted that the final battle between the US and the Islamic Republic will happen soon.

Asia-Pacific media have focused on the US economic boycott campaign, highlighting increased pressure on Iran and its trade partners. Australian and New Zealand media emphasized the fall of the rial, inflation, and medicine shortages. Asian media reported on hidden financial networks, oil smuggling, and sanctions on Chinese and Hong Kong companies.

Omid Memarian, a political analyst, reported an increase in assassinations attributed to the Islamic Republic outside Iran. He stated that the authorities use new methods such as creating fear and threats to suppress opponents. These methods also include planning murders.

Erfan Ghaneifard stated that the US and its intelligence community aim to disrupt operational activities within the IRGC. These actions are intended both to gather information and to create divisions in the IRGC's command structure. These remarks were made amid increased economic pressure from the US.

The US Secretary of Defense stated that the new economic campaign against Iran does not mean the elimination of the military option. He emphasized that "we are by no means ruling out the option of using military attacks in the Strait of Hormuz or around Iran." The US Secretary of Defense also expressed the opinion that Iran cannot withstand the new economic pressure.

The Pakistani army commander discussed with Iranian officials measures to prevent escalation and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The Pakistani interior minister had a positive meeting with the President of the Islamic Republic. This report was published by Javad Hamdani from Iran International.

Mehdi Chamran, head of Tehran City Council, said if the enemy intends to attack again, Iran will preemptively strike. He also mentioned strong resistance in the recent war and pushing the enemy back. These remarks were made during a Tehran City Council session.
Videos received show that despite the fuel station in Gohardasht Karaj being closed with its lights off, cars are lined up to receive gasoline there.

Morteza Kazemian said that US sanctions increase pressure on the Islamic Republic but do not necessarily lead to regime change. The Islamic Republic has learned mechanisms to bypass sanctions and passes economic pressure onto the people. He emphasized that the Iranian people are the main actors in this situation and are absent in the Trump administration's discussions about the sanctions.

Alireza Beiranvand's playing card for Tractor is valid until September 21. If a new letter or inquiry is received, the validity will be extended until the Asian Cup and mid-season. Beiranvand is not included in the preliminary list of the U23 team for the Nagoya Asian Games.

Hamzeh Darvish, a Sunni prisoner in Lakaan Prison in Rasht, was transferred from solitary confinement back to the general ward. This transfer took place on Tuesday, 2 Shahrivar. Previously, he had been held in solitary confinement as a form of punishment.

Videos show that a citizen has made a statue of Aida Aghili on a beach in Oman. Aida Aghili, 34 years old, was shot dead in Tehran on the evening of January 8, 2026. This statue was made in her memory.

The Tehran regional manager of the National Iranian Oil Products Distribution Company stated that a sudden increase in demand caused fuel shortages and temporary closure of some gas stations. On Monday, gasoline distribution in Tehran increased by 30%, with over 26 million liters distributed. This amount set a new record for the current year in the capital.
Farzaneh Tavakoli was killed by gunfire during public protests in Tehran on January 9. The incident involved suppression forces of Khamenei. Her memory remains a guiding light for freedom seekers.

Ali Pishevarzadeh, a water polo athlete and former member of the Chooka Gilan team, has been sentenced to death by the Revolutionary Court of Gilan. After his arrest during the December protests, he was subjected to severe torture and deprived of basic rights. The Human Rights Organization for Sports has reported these facts.

The Israeli Prime Minister claimed that the Islamic Republic tried to kill one of his two sons. He said that if his family were not under security protection, the perpetrators could have succeeded. These statements were made in defense of extending Shin Bet protection for his wife and children.

Sara Rashidi Kachlanlu, a 33-year-old citizen from Maku, was arrested and forcibly disappeared by the Intelligence Organization forces during the December protests. Her family has been unaware of her whereabouts and condition for seven months. Security and judicial authorities in Kermanshah have not provided clear answers to the family's inquiries.

Hossein Alizadeh said the Islamic Republic has put heavy pressure on Gulf oil countries by closing the Strait of Hormuz. He added that Tehran is pursuing a hybrid war and will not limit itself to closing Hormuz. Attacks on US interests and closing Bab al-Mandab are among the options mentioned.

Saadoun Dastar, Rahman Azarakhsh, and Sanan Farasti, three citizens from Oshnavieh, were arrested by security forces. They were transferred to an unknown location. No further details about their situation have been reported.

On the evening of Monday, the 2nd of Shahrivar, the electricity in the entire city of Golbahar in Khorasan Razavi province was cut off. This was reported by a citizen to Iran International. The cause of the power outage has not been announced.

Jafar Pourkabgani stated that the US is trying to create conditions for a military confrontation through economic pressure. He added that the US has so far failed to make the Iranian nation surrender and will not succeed in the future. The only way to stand firm is to rely on self-deterrent capabilities.

Ahmad Alavi, an economics professor, stated that war and international tensions affect market volatility, currency price increases, and inflation. He added that the sharp rise in the dollar price and the fall of the national currency's value after intensified war and sanctions indicate these factors are related to the economic situation.

Mehdi Maskin-Nawaz, a political prisoner in Lakan prison in Rasht, is deprived of proper medical care despite suffering from a herniated disc and needing knee surgery. His family has covered treatment costs, but prison authorities prevent his transfer to medical centers. He was previously burned in Evin prison and now suffers from complications related to that injury.
A citizen reported in a video that they waited 45 minutes in line at a gas station. The station closed before their turn arrived. This issue was reported to Iran International.

A citizen sent a video showing a one-euro coin against a two million rial banknote. He sarcastically calls this the achievement of the Islamic Republic regime after years of rule. The video was sent to Iran International.

The CEO of Total stated that despite tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, transporting crude oil through this route is significantly profitable. He added that sellers' discounts offset transportation costs. These remarks were made in an interview with an Iran International reporter.

Ali Shirazi from Iran International said that gasoline shortages have pushed the Islamic Republic towards reducing quotas and raising prices. The government is concerned about the consequences of this decision, especially street protests. The price increase adds more pressure on people's livelihoods and may escalate protests.

Alireza Beiranvand intends to use his master's thesis defense to obtain a one-year military exemption. If accepted, his conscription will be postponed until February 19, 2027, allowing him to play for Tractor until the end of the 2027 Asian Cup. The military organization has set his conscription date as September 22, and he has until August 25 to transfer to a military team.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International claiming they paid 400,000 tomans for two sheets of pills and received adhesive bandages for the remaining money.

Tottenham has officially signed Savinho, a 22-year-old Brazilian winger from Manchester City, for a base fee of 75 million pounds. With bonuses, the transfer value can reach 85 million pounds, and the contract is valid until 2031. This sale set a new record for the most expensive transfer in Manchester City's history.

Amin Salami visited the grave of the unknown soldier Masoud Zatparvar. He urged people to visit the graves of the unknown soldiers. Amin Salami was killed on January 7, 2026, in Kermanshah, and Masoud Zatparvar died in Rasht.

According to an ILNA report, the base wage of workers decreased from $232 in 2016 to $83 in 2026. The minimum income of a married worker with one child is about $124. Activists report worsening poverty and declining purchasing power among workers and retirees.

Hossein Aghaei stated that the goal of the US economic exclusion operation is to push the Islamic Republic towards economic collapse. He added that economic collapse is a necessary but not sufficient condition for the regime's fall. The meeting between Xi Jinping and Donald Trump in September is important due to China's economic role in the regime's survival.

A group of Iranians living in Italy held a birthday ceremony for Matin Khademi, a deceased Iranian student, in Turin. Matin Khademi was a law student. He ended his life due to psychological pressure following the January 2026 massacre.

The USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier will dock in Thailand next week after more than 200 consecutive days at sea. The ship is heading to Thailand for rest and recreation for sailors and marines. The Thai Navy spokesperson has not yet commented.

A group of current and former football stars issued a statement demanding structural reforms and the removal of FIFA's current management. They criticized Infantino's plans to sell shares of tournaments and said key decisions are made without consulting players and fans. Following the FIFA commercial project crisis, UEFA has called for Infantino's resignation, and some football unions have withdrawn their support.

The United States has begun a new phase of maximum economic pressure against the Islamic Republic since Monday evening, 2 Shahrivar. The US Treasury Secretary called this campaign 'economic exclusion' and the largest financial assault by Washington against Tehran.
A citizen reported that the prices of Sinadaru company's medicines have increased several times. This was reported via a voice message to Iran International. No further details have been provided.

Younes Bakri, Yaser Havasi, and Rouhollah Gholami, three citizens from Asmanabad in Ilam province, were arrested by security forces. These arrests have increased the number of detainees in the area to four. The location where these individuals are held is unknown.

More than 20 security agents simultaneously raided three homes belonging to members of a Bahá'í family in Isfahan and confiscated their personal belongings. The raid took place on August 24 with a judicial warrant. Their instrument-making workshop was also searched, and all tools and valuable handmade instruments were seized.

Ahmad Ardestani stated that people in Iran are dissatisfied with discrimination, bribery, and the role of privileged children but still want the Islamic Republic system to continue. He described the US economic campaign as an attempt to separate the people from the regime and called this idea an illusion. Ardestani emphasized that the government and the people support each other.

Donald Trump described the situation in Iran as a humanitarian crisis on a large scale. He said the Islamic Republic kills protesters even when they are not protesting. Trump called for an immediate stop to this situation.

A memorial birthday ceremony for Azra Bahadorinejad was held at her grave. Azra Bahadorinejad was 39 years old and a mother of two children. She died on the evening of January 9, 2026, in Sabzevar from a direct gunshot by officers.

On Tuesday, 2 Shahrivar, security forces searched the homes and business of the Tabianifard family in Isfahan and sealed their business location. Personal and electronic belongings of the family members were confiscated, and the family members were summoned to security agencies. Their instrument-making workshop and music equipment store were also emptied and seized.

After a 1-0 loss to Tractor, Persepolis players issued a joint message apologizing to fans. They emphasized their commitment to work harder to make up for the result and expressed gratitude for the fans' support. The players stated they will strive until the end to build a team worthy of the Persepolis name.
A video sent on Tuesday, 3rd of Shahrivar, shows a long line of cars at a fuel station in Tehran. The video was sent to Iran International. It concerns the process of receiving gasoline.

A citizen reported in a video to Iran International that they paid 650,000 tomans for one and a half kilograms of fruit. The report highlights severe inflation in Iran. The issue of fruit price increases has been noted.

Roberto Piazza, the Italian head coach of Iran's national volleyball team, announced the team's readiness for the Asian Championship and the four-nation tournament in Russia. He confirmed the policy of youth promotion and team renewal, aiming to qualify for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Piazza also denied rumors about his retirement and explained his delay due to special circumstances and embassy advice.

Hossein Ali Haji Deligani predicted that the US economy will completely collapse within three years. He called for daily broadcasting of this issue by the national media. He also proposed establishing an economic war deputy in the Ministry of Economy and an organization in the Central Bank to counter currency war.
Abbas Araghchi, Iran's Foreign Minister, welcomed Badr Al-Busaidi, Oman's Foreign Minister, in Tehran. This meeting was part of ongoing diplomatic consultations between Iran and Oman.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, stated that all branches of Bank Melli Iran must be closed. The bank has branches in the UAE and Europe that remain operational despite sanctions. Hooman Abedi reported from in front of the Bank Melli branch in London.

On Thursday, August 20, a 50-year-old woman in Saqez was killed by her ex-husband, who later committed suicide after fleeing. Also, a man in Chabahar who killed his 24-year-old wife was arrested by the police.

New images have been released showing the moment bunker-buster missiles hit the glass building of the Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting. This event occurred during the 40-day war. The images related to this incident have been published.

Branko Ivanković posted a picture with Mehdi Taremi and wished him success at Al Wasl. Mehdi Taremi recently joined the Al Wasl team in the UAE. After retiring from coaching, Branko was appointed as the technical director of the UAE national team.

The executive deputy of Masoud Pezeshkian said a decision about gasoline might be made tomorrow or the day after. The head of Masoud Pezeshkian's office confirmed the reduction of gasoline quotas. The 3,000-toman gasoline quota has been reduced from 100 to 50 liters, and another reduction has been confirmed.

Plainclothes officers raided the homes of three members of the Bahá'í community in Isfahan and confiscated their personal belongings and specialized instruments. This information was reported by Iran International. More details will be provided in an interview with Reza Akvanian.

A citizen addressed Abdolnaser Hemmati, the Central Bank governor, in a video claiming there is a dollar shortage and exchange offices are closed. He accused Hemmati of lying about the shortage. The video was sent to Iran International.

The league secretary announced that the spectator quota for the Esteghlal and Persepolis matches is 50-50. Previously, the league spokesperson had said that 90% of the capacity would be allocated to Esteghlal fans. Derby 107 Tehran is scheduled to be held on September 2 at the Naghsh-e Jahan Stadium in Isfahan.

Danny Danon, Israel's representative to the United Nations, welcomed the new US sanctions against the Islamic Republic of Iran. He thanked Donald Trump and Scott Bassett. Danon described increasing economic pressure on Iran as an important and necessary step.

The sentence of 31 lashes for Neda Dadejani and Setayesh Sarabi, detainees of the December 1404 protests, was carried out in the Qorveh criminal court. After the sentence, they were transferred to Sanandaj prison. The sentence was executed on August 22.

In Tehran, the gas station on Seraj Street is closed and diesel is hard to find in eastern Tehran. Water is also cut off for long hours in Tehran. In Bandar Anzali, some people's previous month's fuel quota has been removed without notice.

Two astronauts from NASA and the European Space Agency conducted a spacewalk outside the International Space Station. Anil Menon and Sophie Adeno have started a mission to replace a communication antenna between the station and Earth. This operation is carried out to complete the antenna replacement.

Ali Pishevarzadeh, detained during the December 1404 protests in Rasht, has been sentenced to death by the city's Revolutionary Court. The sentence was issued in the preliminary stage by the second branch of the Rasht Revolutionary Court. Pishevarzadeh was arrested during the protests on December 18 and 19 and is currently held in Lakan Prison in Rasht.

Emanollah Gashtasbi stated that the enemy intended to create insecurity in West Azerbaijan and Kurdistan to carry out a ground invasion. The Islamic Republic's armed and security forces were present in these areas and did not allow enemy infiltration. He emphasized that the armed forces are ready to defend the country and will not allow any aggression.

China's Foreign Ministry stated that cooperation between Beijing and Tehran is conducted according to international laws and should not face interference. The Chinese spokesperson called the US sanctions illegal and said China will take necessary actions to defend its rights. The US has imposed sanctions on 60 individuals, entities, and ships related to Iran.

The US Secret Service announced it is aware of a video that appears to threaten Barron Trump. The video was reportedly aired on Iranian state TV channel 3 and contained information about his residence and movements in New York. A spokesperson said the service investigates any threats against protected individuals.

A citizen reported in a video that the Tehranpars fuel station in Tehran has neither gasoline nor diesel. This report was sent on Tuesday, 3rd of Shahrivar. The fuel shortage at this station has been confirmed.

The director general of education in Kerman province announced a shortage of 4,500 classrooms in the province. Of these, 1,000 classrooms belong to the city of Kerman. Additionally, about 20% of the schools in the province are dilapidated and need renovation.

Donald Trump announced that the US Navy has cleared or detonated all mines in the international waters of the Strait of Hormuz. He warned that any ship or boat laying new mines will be destroyed. Trump also stated that the US Space Force is monitoring the Strait of Hormuz and several nuclear sites.

Donald Trump stated that the Islamic Republic of Iran is not paying the salaries of its military forces and is killing protesters on an unprecedented scale. He described this situation as a massive humanitarian crisis and called for it to stop immediately.

A female prisoner named Zahra Azizpour was executed in Lakaan Prison in Rasht. The sentence was carried out on the early morning of Tuesday, 3 Shahrivar. Zahra Azizpour was about 43 years old and from Ardabil.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated that the Security Council's decision to accept and sign the agreement was made with coordination among the heads of powers and based on collective wisdom. He emphasized that the signing was based on logic and awareness, not fear. Pezeshkian also said that US economic pressure to force Iran to surrender will be ineffective.

Jalal Mashhadi Mohammad, a 62-year-old protester, was killed by a sniper's direct shot during the December protests in Tehran. His family found his body after a long search in the Mehrab Karizak hall. His son was under heavy security pressure before receiving the body to be identified as a Basij force member.

Faeq Zidan, head of Iraq's Supreme Judicial Council, met with Masoud Pezeshkian and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf in Tehran. Pezeshkian emphasized the importance of Islamic countries' convergence for regional security and peace. He also mentioned enemies' attempts to create discord among regional countries.
A citizen reported rising prices in Iran in a video to Iran International. He said the price of 10 eggs, a small bottle of oil, and two cans of beans reached 1,170,000 tomans.

Foolad Mobarakeh Sepahan club condemned the insulting behavior of Aref Hajiaidi after the match against Esteghlal and apologized to the club and its fans. Hajiaidi accepted responsibility for his behavior and expressed regret. Sepahan club emphasized that appropriate disciplinary actions will be taken and called for fair treatment of disciplinary cases.

Mohammad Reza Aref stated that the Islamic Republic of Iran is fully prepared to confront the enemy. He added that the Islamic Republic was also prepared for previous wars with the US and Israel. These remarks were made in an interview with Masoud Pezeshkian's first deputy.

The Sports Human Rights Organization announced that Ali Pishevarzadeh, an athlete and former member of the Chooka Gilan water polo team, is at risk of execution. This issue was discussed in an interview with Zohreh Abdollahkhani, a researcher of international sports policies.

Arman Moghari, a 32-year-old resident of Rasht, has been detained by security forces for over three months and is held in Lakaan Prison in Rasht. His case, involving security charges, is under review at the second branch of the Revolutionary Court of Rasht. This detention continues without a final court decision.

Oman and the Islamic Republic of Iran discussed resuming safe shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. They reviewed a phased framework including a temporary corridor and mine clearance. Technical negotiations for a permanent corridor and ship traffic management will continue.

Ahmad Samadi reported that a third drone carrying about 50 grams of a suspicious substance called hexogen was found near Leipzig-Halle airport. This discovery is linked to the failed drone attack case. German security sources suggested possible involvement of Russian intelligence, which Moscow has denied.

The US Treasury Department has sanctioned the Singaporean company Welbred Capital and its affiliates in the UAE, Switzerland, and France. Washington claims this network is linked to Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani and transports Iranian and Russian oil to global markets. Additionally, an Italian newspaper reported on the fall of the rial's value and the economic crisis's impact on daily life in Iran.

Several fuel stations in Tehran have been closed due to a sudden increase in demand. The manager of the National Iranian Oil Products Distribution Company cited delays in deliveries and fuel shortages at some stations as the cause. Gasoline distribution in Tehran has increased by 30%, and fuel supply continues to be stable.

Iran and Oman issued a joint statement on resuming safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. The foreign ministers discussed a phased framework to manage the current situation in the strait. Technical negotiations will continue to establish a permanent corridor and manage maritime traffic.

Scott Bessent, US Treasury Secretary, said Iranian leaders are admitting that pressure is working. He quoted President Masoud Pezeshkian as saying war must end at some point, and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf as saying that without economic growth, military power cannot be sustained. Bessent stressed that under Trump, the Treasury will continue to cut off economic lifelines until Tehran is isolated.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said statements by Islamic Republic officials show that economic pressure on Tehran is taking effect. He pointed to remarks by Masoud Pezeshkian about economic shortages and the need to end the war, as well as statements by Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf. Bessent stressed that the US Treasury will continue to cut off any economic lifeline keeping the Islamic Republic afloat so that Tehran is left alone.

Esmaeil Baqaei, spokesperson of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, reacted to the major economic operation by the US against Tehran. He described these actions as violations of international law principles and the UN Charter. Baqaei also mentioned Canada as a country learning this lesson.

Meningitis has spread to most wards in Dastgerd prison in Isfahan. Several prisoners have been transferred to the hospital, and reports of some deaths have been published. Prison authorities have canceled visitations and provided masks to prisoners, but the disease continues to spread.

Badr Al Busaidi, Oman’s foreign minister, expressed hope for the soon establishment of a temporary corridor in the Strait of Hormuz and practical arrangements for safe shipping. He stated that talks on the future management of the Strait will continue under the Islamabad agreement. Oman will also continue consultations with regional partners to maintain freedom of navigation.

The Harana report shows that between July 11 and July 31, 2026, at least 72 popular pages were blocked and 23 business units were closed. These actions are part of a new phase of social control policies occurring alongside the de-escalation of the war in Iran. The reported numbers represent minimum confirmed cases and also include page purges and content removals in various cities.

Mehdi Taremi held his first training session with Al Wasl after joining the UAE club. He is preparing for his first official match against Shabab Al Ahli, which has several Iranian players. Previously, Taremi played for Olympiacos and scored 16 goals last season.

A citizen in a video referred to the high prices of essential goods and sarcastically used the nickname "cardboard leader" for Mojtaba Khamenei. He said the country is run with cardboard. This video was sent to Iran International.

Miad Maleki commented on Donald Trump's statements about the possible collapse of the Islamic Republic. He said that the decline in purchasing power could lead to new crises and protests. He also noted that printing money might pay salaries but economic problems would persist.

Oston Urunov, the Uzbek player of Persepolis, was injured in a friendly match from the hamstring area. The exact extent of the injury and his recovery time are not yet known, and he will undergo an MRI tomorrow. His participation in the capital derby is currently uncertain.

Rouhollah Rahimpour pointed to the increased concern of Islamic Republic officials about a new wave of protests amid the worsening economic crisis. He said this situation is accompanied by intensified internal conflicts and power struggles within the government. He added that the new protests could deepen internal divisions.

Recep Tayyip Erdogan stated that as the shock from tensions between the Islamic Republic and the US on the global economy gradually decreases, its effects on people's daily lives will become clearer. He also said Turkey's active foreign policy prioritizing regional peace and stability has worried groups benefiting from instability.

Axios, quoting two American officials, reported that the US Navy has cleared mines from the central shipping lane between Iran and Oman in the Strait of Hormuz. These officials confirmed Donald Trump's earlier statements that all mines in the international waters of the Strait of Hormuz had been collected or detonated. According to Axios, US Navy underwater drones had identified over 100 suspicious objects resembling mines.

Following a fire at the Iran Cola beverage factory in Iranshahr, the factory has been shut down. Ninety workers employed there are now uncertain about their status. The future operation of the factory is unclear.

Trump stated that the Strait of Hormuz is completely open. He also said that every inch of Iran's nuclear sites is under surveillance. These remarks were made in the audio version of Titrawol with Niusha Saremi.

Iranians living in the UK held a protest on Tuesday in front of the Prime Minister's office in London against the execution of prisoners and political protesters in Iran. This protest was reported through a video received by Iran International.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said in a meeting with Faiq Zidan that Iran and Iraq have a decisive role in the new regional order. He called for the complete withdrawal of US coalition forces from Iraq. Ghalibaf also emphasized that the US has failed in military, political, and economic wars.

Hedayat Mombini announced that Amir Ghalenoei will continue as the head coach of Iran's national football team until the Asian Championship. The board will receive a report on Ghalenoei's performance and plans tomorrow. The federation expects the national team to become champion or finalist in this tournament.

A citizen living in southern Iran sent a video to Iran International saying that electricity is cut off daily and constantly, and despite low household consumption, the electricity bill has reached 2.4 million tomans.

Abbas Pazouki stated that gasoline quotas will remain unchanged at least until the end of Shahrivar and there will be no immediate or sudden shock implementation. Any future plans will be communicated to the public in advance. Some government officials have been seriously warned regarding recent gasoline-related statements.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International complaining about the high price of carrots. He addressed Mojtaba Khamenei, saying the government has left no healthy land in the country. The video highlights the deteriorating agricultural situation.
A citizen has shared a video showing a long gasoline queue on the Tehran-Karaj highway. The video was sent on Tuesday. The fuel crisis in Iran continues.

Alireza Zakani, the mayor of Tehran, stated that the country's resources are sufficient to meet people's livelihoods for at least the next three months. He also said that to compensate for the budget deficit, the country must be managed like in wartime.

The UK Treasury Minister announced that the UK government has imposed over 240 sanctions against the Islamic Republic. The UK continues to cooperate with the US to increase economic pressure. London is determined to prevent Iran from using the UK financial system.

Ali Nikzad, the deputy speaker of the parliament, announced the reduction of two gasoline quotas. The 70-liter quota will be reduced to 50 liters and the 30-liter quota to 15 liters. The 1500-toman gasoline price will be maintained, and the fourth gasoline rate has been rejected.

Sixty teachers and activists protested the detention conditions of Masoud Farhikhteh, a teacher imprisoned in Karaj Central Prison. Since his transfer, he has been moved multiple times to solitary confinement or unknown locations, and his contact with family has been cut off. The signatories hold the prison organization and judiciary responsible for his situation.

Marco Rubio stated that the US currently does not expect new aggressive attacks on Iran and is focusing on increasing economic pressure and normalizing shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Military action is not ruled out if new conflicts start from Iran. This approach will continue at least until the US midterm elections.

Erfan Ghaneifard, a Middle East analyst, spoke about the US Secret Service investigation into the Islamic Republic's video threatening Barron Trump. He said the name of the Islamic Republic is again linked to threats and extraterritorial operations. This issue has become a serious national security concern for the US.

Reuters reported, citing American media, that John Ratcliffe, CIA director, traveled to Moscow to meet with Russian officials. CBS News and Axios reported the trip citing anonymous sources, but details of the meetings and the topics of discussion have not been released. If confirmed, this would be the first visit by a CIA director to Moscow since November 2021.

Gas in Fereydunshahr was cut off for one hour, and after restoration, a gas smell spread in the city. Electricity in Sanandaj was cut off without notice at 22:20. People reported economic difficulties, rising medicine prices, and a shortage of infant formula in Rasht.

Mahmoud Nabavian, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, criticized the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic for violating the management of the Strait of Hormuz. He questioned on what authorization the Foreign Minister violated Mojtaba Khamenei's order regarding exclusive management of the Strait. Nabavian also criticized the creation of consensus against the Islamic Republic due to Iran's management in the southern corridor.

Aram Hesami, a political science professor, commented on the economic expulsion operation by the Trump administration against the Islamic Republic. He said the success of this operation depends on the cooperation of countries like China, UAE, Russia, India, and Turkey. Without their cooperation, effective maximum pressure will be difficult.

Kazem Gharibabadi stated that the entry route to the Persian Gulf will be through Iranian waters and the exit through Omani waters. This route is temporary, and the two countries will negotiate a permanent route within 30 to 60 days. Military vessels are prohibited from passing, and only commercial ships are allowed to transit.

Bruno Fernandes, captain of Manchester United, won the Professional Footballers' Association (PFA) Player of the Year award for 2026. He played a key role in Manchester United's third-place finish with 21 assists and 9 goals. Additionally, Nico O'Reilly from Manchester City received the Young Player of the Year award.

TankerTrackers announced that at least 15 ship-to-ship transfer operations are underway in the Sea of Oman. These operations involve about 25 million barrels of crude oil and some petroleum products. The oil being transferred is from almost all regional countries except Iran.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Speaker of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, criticized the remarks of US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent about new sanctions against Iran by posting a part of his press conference video on X. Ghalibaf pointed to the contradiction in Bessent's words and called it a comedy show.

John Healy, the UK Treasury Secretary, announced that the UK government will continue economic pressure on the Islamic Republic of Iran alongside the US and partners. The UK has imposed over 240 sanctions on Iran and will take action to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. It also supports US efforts for a diplomatic solution.

Bloomberg reported that the new US warning about sanctions on countries trading with Iran has put Turkey at risk of losing gas imports from Iran. Last year, Turkey sourced 13% of its imported gas from Iran. The US is likely to consult with Turkish leaders on this issue.

Kazem Gharibabadi, the deputy foreign minister, stated that the Islamic Republic can take preemptive actions to defend its interests. He said if the US targets Iran's economic interests, Iran will also target US economic interests.

The Israeli army and internal security agency announced they targeted several locations in Gaza. These sites were storing rockets, weapons, and ammunition. The weapon depots were located inside mosques and near humanitarian infrastructure.

The Institute for Science and International Security reported the identification of a possible underground facility at the Natanz nuclear complex. This facility may be intended for storing uranium hexafluoride cylinders and supporting large-scale enrichment. Construction began in 2010 and the main part was completed between 2015 and 2017.

Tom Barrack announced that Donald Trump's plan for the Middle East has entered an important phase. He said Trump's policy has facilitated the integration of the Syrian Democratic Forces into Syrian government institutions. Barrack mentioned the role of Kurds in the Syrian government and the recognition of the Kurdish language.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf called Scott Bassett's remarks a ridiculous show and a clown day. Bassett had previously described new sanctions against Iran as decisive. Ghalibaf said the program was not like the Normandy operation and described it as a ridiculous stand-up.

Marco Rubio stated that the US currently does not expect new attacks against the Islamic Republic and is focusing on economic pressure, naval blockade, and new sanctions. The US does not intend to return to large-scale military operations but does not rule out military action if attacked by the Islamic Republic. Washington is not negotiating with Tehran and aims to increase pressure to bring the Islamic Republic back to the negotiating table.

After the dollar price rose to 200,000 tomans, supporters of the Islamic Republic held nightly gatherings in Tehran, chanting slogans against Abdolnaser Hemmati and Masoud Pezeshkian. These gatherings were shared on social media. The protests are related to the economic situation and the responsible officials.

The Washington Post reported that Donald Trump's tariffs and the war with the Islamic Republic have increased the costs of fertilizer, fuel, and agricultural machinery. Congressional efforts for emergency aid to farmers have stalled, and some groups oppose linking aid to war funding. The National Farmers Union warned that war funding could increase economic pressure on farmers.

Financial Times reported a daily shortage of about 15 million liters of gasoline in Iran. Images and messages indicate long queues and station closures in Tehran, Karaj, and other cities. People are moving from one gas station to another with empty tanks.

NBC News reported that missile and drone attacks by the Islamic Republic on US facilities in the Middle East caused billions of dollars in damage. These attacks revealed weaknesses in the defense systems of US bases. US officials are reconsidering how to protect sensitive intelligence and surveillance facilities in the region.

Ahmad Al-Sharrah and Mazlum Abdi met in Damascus to discuss the integration of the Syrian Democratic Forces into government institutions. Abdi announced the end of the SDF's mission and its merger with the Syrian army. Kurdish language education will also start this year.

Shayan Samiei stated that the US mine-clearing operation in the Strait of Hormuz has ended. Trump's threat to destroy mine-laying vessels indicates Washington's effort to control international waters. The goal is to establish a security regime managed by the US in the Strait of Hormuz.

The Syrian Foreign Ministry condemned the entry of Israeli Defense Minister Yisrael Katz into Syrian territory as a violation of sovereignty and international laws. Damascus called on the international community to act to stop these violations and urged Israeli forces to withdraw and return to the separation line. Katz stated that the Israeli army will not withdraw from the area as long as jihadist threats continue.

The US government has temporarily suspended or rescheduled visa interview appointments at its embassies and consulates. This action is due to a training program for consular staff. The US State Department has not provided details on the duration of the program or when appointments will return to normal.

The US naval blockade has kept oil tankers flying the Iranian flag away from Iranian ports. At least 20 empty tankers have anchored near Sri Lanka after ship-to-ship oil transfers in Southeast Asia. Additionally, 26 other tankers have been tracked in the Singapore Strait and are expected to conduct ship-to-ship transfers near Malaysia.

Iraq's Foreign Ministry summoned Mohammad Kazem Al-Sadegh, Iran's ambassador in Baghdad, to explain the publication of regional maps. The Iraqi deputy foreign minister emphasized continued consultations and resolving disputes through diplomacy. Both sides discussed strengthening bilateral relations and various cooperation.

Amir Mohammad Golvani warned that if current conditions persist or military conflicts resume, the dollar rate could increase by 25 to 50 percent by the end of the year. He attributed the rise in exchange rates to chronic inflation, liquidity growth, and war damages. Golvani stated that only a political breakthrough or agreement can change expectations.

Italian media reported on the fall of the rial's value and the rise in essential goods prices in Iran. Corriere della Sera wrote that economic pressure has forced many Iranian households to remove meat and some other items from their tables. The report was prepared by Sadaf Baghbani from Iran International.

Marco Rubio stated that the US currently does not intend to start a new round of military attacks against the Islamic Republic. The Trump administration is focusing on increasing economic pressure, naval blockade, and new sanctions. This information was reported by Iran International.

Mohammad Qaedi considers the halt of attacks against the Islamic Republic as a tactical pause. Economic pressure and naval blockade continue. Internal concerns in the US about fuel prices, inflation, and midterm elections influenced this decision.

Alireza Namvar Haghighi reported increasing economic and livelihood pressures in Iran. He mentioned rising inflation, dollar prices, energy problems, and retirees' protests. He warned that continuing this situation could increase political divides and social protests.

The group Opium Moon, with members from Iran, Israel, and the USA, has released an album called "The Time Has Come." The album focuses on peace, empathy, and staying together during crises. Music serves as their common language amid war and politics.
